summary: Storyteller is a client-server application generating short audio stories for preschool kids from voice input. The React client records audio and sends it as a buffer to a custom Fastify server, which communicates results back via server-sent events. The pipeline begins with OpenAI Whisper transcription (~1.5 seconds), followed by GPT-3.5 Turbo Instruct generating a story outline (~4 seconds). Once the outline exists, three tasks run in parallel: title generation (GPT-3.5 Turbo Instruct), image generation (GPT-4 extracts keywords, Stability AI Stable Diffusion XL generates the image), and full audio story generation. Audio story generation is the bottleneck at ~1.5 minutes using GPT-4 with low temperature to produce structured dialogue with speakers. To address this latency, ModelFusion streams partially parsed JSON structures; the application narrates each story part as it completes. For voice selection, GPT-3.5 generates a gender and voice description per speaker, and pre-embedded voice descriptions are retrieved via similarity search filtered by gender, ensuring no duplicate voices. Speech synthesis uses supported providers including ElevenLabs. Generated audio and image files are stored virtually on the server with paths sent to the client, enabling playback to begin while generation continues. The recap highlights responsiveness through streaming, parallelism, incremental UI updates, and model choices that minimize processing time. ModelFusion provides type inference, partial JSON parsing of streamed fragments, and multi-modal model support beyond text. The talk concludes with GitHub links to both the Storyteller app and the ModelFusion library.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: Storyteller generates ~2-minute preschool audio stories from voice input using a multi-model TypeScript pipeline orchestrated by ModelFusion.
Responsiveness is the primary engineering challenge, addressed via streaming, parallel processing, incremental UI updates, and early playback.
OpenAI Whisper transcribes short topics in ~1.5 seconds; GPT-3.5 Turbo Instruct generates story outlines in ~4 seconds.
After the outline, title generation, image generation, and audio story generation all run in parallel.
GPT-4 with low temperature produces structured dialogue/speaker data but takes ~1.5 minutes, necessitating streaming partial JSON parsing via ModelFusion.
ModelFusion returns an iterable over fragments of partially parsed results, letting the app narrate each completed story part immediately.
Speaker voices are selected by generating a gender and voice description with GPT-3.5, then retrieving via embedding similarity filtered by gender to avoid duplicates.
Images use GPT-4 keyword extraction feeding Stability AI Stable Diffusion XL; audio synthesis uses ElevenLabs; both store virtual server files referenced by the client.
Client-server communication uses server-sent events so the React UI updates as each result becomes available.
ModelFusion's key features demonstrated include type inference, comprehensive control, integrated tooling, and support for non-text modalities.

sections.title: Introduction and Story Example
sections.summary: Lars introduces Storyteller, a TypeScript and ModelFusion app generating ~2-minute audio stories for preschool kids from voice input, and plays an example story excerpt with dialogue.

sections.title: Architecture and Main Challenges
sections.summary: Storyteller is a client-server app: React frontend and custom Fastify backend. Main challenges are responsiveness, quality, and consistency.

sections.title: Recording and Transcription
sections.summary: Client records audio, sends buffer to server; OpenAI Whisper transcribes in ~1.5 seconds; results sent back via server-sent events updating React state.

sections.title: Story Outline and Parallel Task Launch
sections.summary: GPT-3.5 Turbo Instruct generates a story outline in ~4 seconds; once available, title, image, and audio story generation start in parallel.

sections.title: Title and Image Generation
sections.summary: Title uses GPT-3.5 Turbo Instruct quickly. For images, GPT-4 extracts representative keywords from the story, passed to Stability AI Stable Diffusion XL; the image is stored virtually and served to the client.

sections.title: Audio Story Generation and Streaming
sections.summary: GPT-4 with low temperature generates structured dialogue with speakers in ~1.5 minutes. ModelFusion streams partially parsed fragments; the app narrates each finished story part immediately to address latency.

sections.title: Speaker Voice Selection
sections.summary: For each new speaker, GPT-3.5 generates a gender and voice description; pre-embedded voices are retrieved by similarity filtered by gender, ensuring no duplicate voices across speakers.

sections.title: Speech Synthesis and Client Playback
sections.summary: Speech synthesis uses supported providers including ElevenLabs; audio files stored virtually and served to client; playback begins after first audio completes while server continues generating.

sections.title: Recap and Conclusion
sections.summary: Responsiveness is achieved via incremental loading states, streaming, parallel backend processing, early playback, and model choices minimizing generation time. Lars points to GitHub repos for Storyteller and ModelFusion.

demonstrations: Example story excerpt about Benny the forest animal showing narrative style and dialogue
Walkthrough of the full Storyteller pipeline from voice recording to audio playback

GPT-3.5 Turbo Instruct generates a story outline in about 4 seconds
